subject: Cloud Computing
title: Storage Tiers and Cold Storage
description: A quick, practical guide to Storage Tiers and Cold Storage.

hook.text: Not all data is accessed equally. Some files haven't been touched in years. Why store them expensively?

buildup.text: Cloud providers offer storage tiers: hot for frequent access, warm for occasional, cold for archives.

discovery.text: AWS Glacier stores data for as little as $1 per terabyte per month. The catch: retrieval takes hours.

twist.text: Many companies waste money storing rarely-used data on expensive hot tiers out of laziness.

climax.text: Smart tiering policies automatically move data to cheaper storage as it ages. Set it and forget it.

punchline.text: Cold storage is cheap but slow. Most old data can wait.

quiz.question: What is the trade-off of using cold storage like AWS Glacier?
options: It's extremely cheap but retrieving data can take hours
It's free but limited to 1 gigabyte per account
It's fast but deletes data automatically after 30 days

details.summary: Cloud providers offer multiple storage tiers at different price points based on access frequency. Hot storage for frequently accessed data costs more, while cold and archive storage offer massive savings for data that is rarely accessed but must be retained.
details.whyItMatters: Most organizations store vast amounts of data they rarely access. Moving infrequently used data to colder tiers can cut storage costs by up to 95% without losing accessibility.
takeaways: Hot, warm, cold, and archive tiers serve different access patterns
Archive storage like Glacier costs pennies per gigabyte per month
Lifecycle policies can automate transitions between tiers

faq.question: What is the cheapest cloud storage option?
faq.answer: Archive storage like AWS Glacier Deep Archive costs roughly $1 per terabyte per month but has retrieval times of hours. Standard Glacier costs slightly more but retrieves in minutes to hours. These tiers are ideal for compliance archives, backups, and data retained for legal reasons.

faq.question: How do lifecycle policies work?
faq.answer: Lifecycle policies automatically move objects between storage tiers based on age. For example, data might stay in hot storage for 30 days, move to warm for 90 days, then to cold or archive. This optimizes costs automatically without manual intervention.
